  journalctl --user -u spark-console-api -n 30 --no-pager 2>&1 | sed 's/^/    /' >&2 || true
  exit 1
}
FIRST=''
END=$((SECONDS + WAIT_S))
while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$END" ]; do
  FIRST=$(socket_health | started "$API_BUILD") && break
  FIRST=''; sleep 1
done
[ -n "$FIRST" ] || miss "it didn't answer on its socket within $WAIT_S seconds"
echo "  health: ok (build $API_BUILD). Watching that it keeps running for $SETTLE_S seconds ..."
same_process() {
  local now quiet=0
  while :; do
    now=$(socket_health | started "$API_BUILD") || now=''
    [ -z "$now" ] || { [ "$now" = "$FIRST" ]; return; }
    quiet=$((quiet + 1)); [ "$quiet" -lt 3 ] || return 1
    sleep 2
  done
}
END=$((SECONDS + SETTLE_S))
while [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$END" ]; do
  sleep 2
  same_process || miss "it stopped or restarted by itself in its first $SETTLE_S seconds"
done
if [ -n "$OWNER" ]; then
  check_ways || miss "$WHY"
  echo "  ways in: ok (sign-in, the agent door, the model address)"
  if [ "$CHAT_CHECK" = yes ]; then
    check_chat || miss "$WHY"
    echo "  chat: ok (Sparkie called a tool and answered)"
  else
    echo "  chat: not checked ($CHAT_WHY)"
  fi
else
  echo "  No owner is set up yet, so sign-in and chat weren't checked."
fi
if [ "$TG_BEFORE" = ok ]; then
  END=$((SECONDS + SETTLE_S))
  until [ "$(socket_health | field telegram)" = ok ]; do
    [ "$SECONDS" -lt "$END" ] || miss "Telegram was working before this update and isn't polling now"
    sleep 2
  done
  echo "  Telegram: ok (polling again)"
fi
same_process || miss "it restarted by itself during the checks"
PHASE=done
echo "  kept: build $API_BUILD passed its checks"

specs.risk:
- A test that runs an installer can touch the real machine. Guard: only the extracted Spark 2 half is run, in a temp HOME, with stand-ins first on PATH; ssh, sudo, tailscale and systemd-run stand-ins fail closed and the test asserts they were never called; DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS is emptied so a real `systemctl --user` could not reach the user manager. The Mac half (tailscale serve, sudo) is never run by a test.
- The trap must not put files back when nothing changed, or after the checks passed. Guard: PHASE (before, snapshot, changing, done) and cases 7, 8, 9 ("nothing changed") and 1.
- set -e traps in new code: every substitution that may fail is in an `&&`/`||` list or ends in `|| true`; check functions set WHY and return 1. The `check` mode's output must stay untouched (the Mac half reads its last line).
- A good build sent back by mistake. Sources and guards: one odd model answer (second try in a new chat); slow /v1/models when Sparks are off (60 s limit); Telegram blip (compared only if it was ok before, and given 40 s more); a cut session during the 40 s wait (the next echo fails and the build goes back: safe, the owner runs it again). The owner's override for the brain-dependent check is SKIP_CHAT_CHECK=1. A wrong check can always be fixed by the next install, because install.sh travels with the new files.
- The chat check leaves one chat in the owner's list (it cannot delete without the passkey). It is reused until 150 messages, then a new one is made; if the owner has 300 chats and none is the check's, the chat check misses and says so.
- `same` instead of comparing build ids is a deliberate change from the report's wording: the build id covers three files, so a page-only or config-only update would have been skipped by undo. After an update that was put back automatically, "undo the last update" now goes to the build before that one (as the report intended); the stamp is in the question and the notice.
- restore.sh still empties the live folder before copying; with a full disk the put-back itself can fail. It now ends with the unit started and the free-space check runs first; the rename-swap was cut by the review and stays cut.
- bash 3.2 on the Mac versus bash 5 on Spark 2: the tested paths behaved the same in a scratch dry run, but the Mac run uses tar and find shims. A Linux run of the same file is the full proof.
- macOS socket paths over 104 characters fail with EINVAL (seen in the scratch run): keep the test HOME short.
- An update takes about 1.5 to 2.5 minutes longer (40 s settle, the model list, one chat turn).
- Same file as H1, S5 and S11: H1's go-back.sh must pick "newest folder with restore.sh and no same"; S5 can read the snapshot's `build` file. The tree is being edited by others right now (18-workflows.mjs changed at 22:59): find lastSnapshot by name.
- Not covered by this item: a crash more than about a minute after the checks end (H3 and the watchdog), state changed by the new build before it is put back (S12), SIGKILL or power loss mid-copy.

- R29, rewrite: "`node test/lock.mjs` passes on the exact tree before installing; every action is in `TOOLS` or `CHANGE_TOOLS`. specs.risk:
1. A skipped save leaves the list one change behind until the next change. A stop that finishes during a failed read stays on the list and shows as held ("should be running but isn’t"), which the owner clears with Forget; a start that finishes then is missing from the list (not healed, not undoable). For a two-Spark model the stale entry can be started again by self-healing once the 15-minute "stopped on purpose" mark runs out. That is the fault F24 (backlog) fixes; this item adds a rare new way to reach it. Guard: it needs a read error at the exact moment an operation ends, the service log says so, and today's behaviour in the same moment is worse (the whole list and its history are wiped). No retry on purpose: a late retry could apply an old stop after a newer start.
2. recordWorkflowRun must not throw: runJob calls it bare, so a throw would skip the list update, the chat result and the event, and become an unhandled rejection. Guard: the catch and return inside the function; the test waits for the operation's "completed" event, which is written after it.
3. A skipped record must not announce "Validated". Guard: the read is the first thing after the cancelled check, and the return comes before the notice.
4. The test must use a link to a folder, not a plain folder and not chmod 000 (a plain folder passes without the fix; chmod does nothing as root). It relies on rename replacing a link, which is standard on Linux and macOS and was probed on this Mac.
5. Lookups stay tolerant by design, so after a failed read should_be_running shows an empty list and undo says there is nothing to undo for that one call. Not made worse here; not part of F12.
6. state.test.mjs gains a fourth service running beside the other three; its time limits scale with SPARK_TEST_SLOW like its neighbours.

All three halves are unchanged in the current tree (line numbers still match the report). Page only; the service side is already right.

1. Locked phone loses the answer - public/app.js `sendConsole` (line 4005). Its catch (4035-4037) toasts the raw `e.message` and drops the half-written reply: `c.conv.messages = (c.conv.messages || []).filter(m => !m.streaming)`. A stream that ends without `done` (4033) only sets "The connection closed before the answer finished." and then (4035) swaps in the saved chat once; while the service is still answering that copy has no reply, so the partial text vanishes and nothing waits. Only `openConsole` (3984) waits on `conv.replying`. Afterwards `send()` (4074-4078) calls `watchOps`, which stops at once when no operation is pending (3934). `streamChat` (2444) takes no signal, so a read that hangs leaves `state.chat.sending` true until reload.
2. Failed send wipes the words - `sendConsole` clears the box before the request (4012 `ta.value = c.draft = ''`) and never puts it back; the local user message stays on screen though the service never stored it. `streamChat` (2444-2449) calls `fetch` with no try/catch, so the toast is the browser's own text ("Load failed" / "Failed to fetch"). A 409/429 loses the words the same way.
3. One missed poll marks a job failed - `followServiceJob` (2395), line 2411: `if (e.status === 404 || e.missing) { j = { ...j, status: 'failed', error: e.message }; break; }`, then the "... failed" toast. `activityJobs` (427-429) lets that local copy win over the service's list.

Service facts the fix relies on (no service change needed): service/src/14-chats.mjs `chatReply` sets `link.detached` on close and the turn finishes and is saved; `sparkieTurn` saves the user message (trimmed text) before `emit({type:'started'})`; `chatSummary` carries `replying`; service/src/24-handler.mjs chat branch answers `GET /chats/<id>` with `{...chatSummary(conv), messages}`; `GET /jobs/<id>` answers 404 "That operation has expired." for a job it no longer has. The service sends no heartbeat while the brain thinks or a tool runs (so a "no bytes for 60 s" timer would cut healthy streams).

New file /Users/akuppala/Documents/26aiRAG/spark-console/test/page.test.mjs (if another item has already created it, append). It runs the page's real functions without a browser. It starts NO stand-in fleet: F19 changes no service code, so `fetch` and the service's answers are faked inside the test (node:test, node:assert/strict, node:fs, node:vm only; `waitFor` and `SLOW` from ./lib.mjs for waits, `{ every: 5, timeout: 3000 }`; never fixed sleeps, never an unbounded wait loop).

Harness (about 50 lines):
- `LINES` = public/app.js split on newlines. `pageFn(name)`: find the line matching `^\s*(async )?function name\(`, assert it exists, take its indent, end at the first later line that is exactly indent + `}`; return those lines joined.
- `page({ fetch, saved, jobs })`: build an object `p`, `vm.createContext(p)`, then `vm.runInContext(['streamChat','savedAnswer','sendConsole','followServiceJob'].map(pageFn).join('\n'), p)`. Stand-ins on `p`: `c = { conv: { id: 'sc_0123456789ab', messages: [] }, draft: '', sending: false, spark: null }`, `ta = { value: '' }`, `layout = { isConnected: true }`, `state = { main: { data: null }, svcJobs: new Map() }`, `document = { hidden: false, addEventListener/removeEventListener that keep 'visibilitychange' handlers in p.wake }`, `fetch` (counts calls in p.posts, then the case's fake), `capi(path)` (for `chats/<id>` records a copy of `p.c.conv.messages` in p.seen and answers the next item of `saved`, the last one repeating, throwing it if it is an Error; for `jobs/…` the same from `jobs`), `toast` (pushes `{message, kind}` to p.toasts), `sleep = () => new Promise(r => setImmediate(r))`, `CONSOLE_API`, `ASSISTANT: 'Sparkie'`, `SVC_LABEL: {}`, `dismissedToasts: new Set()`, `underWay`, `TextDecoder`, `AbortController`, `history: { replaceState() {} }`, `subjectNode: () => null`, `fleetSnapshot: () => 'snapshot'`, `sparkSnapshot`, `jobPercent: () => null`, `num`, `plural`, `canRun: () => false`, `$: () => null`, `h: () => ({})`, and no-ops for grow, drawHead, drawMessages, drawComposer, drawSoon, announce, followNewJobs, loadConsoleChats, runLive, openActivity, loadJobs, loadLibrary, loadRecipes, loadMain, loadMainChoices, loadStatus.
- `stream(events, then)`: a fake fetch answering 200 whose reader gives the events as one SSE chunk, then 'cut' (read rejects with `TypeError('Load failed')`), 'end' (`{done:true}`), or 'hang' (never settles; rejects with an AbortError when the passed `signal` aborts).
- Objects made inside the vm context are another realm: compare strings, numbers and lengths with `assert.equal`, never `deepEqual` on them.

Cases (TEXT = 'start glm on spark 3'; user = saved user message with that content; answer = saved assistant message 'Half and the rest.'; half = [{type:'started'},{type:'delta',text:'Half '}]):
1. Cut mid-stream: fetch = stream(half,'cut'); saved = replying:true [user] twice, then replying:false [user, answer]. After `await p.sendConsole(TEXT)`: last message content is the answer; the last p.seen snapshot's last message is 'Half ' (kept while waiting); c.sending false; ta.value ''; p.posts 1; no toast matching /Load failed|Failed to fetch|aborted/i.
2. Stream closes early ('end'): same end state.
3. Stream goes quiet ('hang'), saved = replying:false [user, answer]: start sendConsole, wait until the last message is 'Half ', assert c.sending true and p.wake.length 1, call the wake handler, await: answer shown, c.sending false, p.wake.length 0, no raw-error toast.
4. Coming back on screen does not cut a live stream: a reader whose second read resolves only when the test releases it (then delta + done); saved = replying:true twice, then finished. Call the wake handler, wait for two saved reads, assert the last message is still 'Half '; release; await: answer shown and p.toasts.length 0.
5. A message the service never got goes back in the box, for four variants: fetch rejects 'Failed to fetch' with an empty saved chat; fetch rejects 'Load failed' with the saved read also failing; a 502 with a non-JSON body; a 409 `{error:'Sparkie is still answering in this conversation.'}`. Each: ta.value and c.draft equal TEXT, messages.length 0, c.sending false, p.posts 1, exactly one toast, its text matching /^Can’t reach Spark Console’s service\./ (first two), the restart sentence (502), the service's own sentence (409).

specs.risk:
- Sending a change twice. Guard: the page never resends; the words go back only when the saved chat does not hold the message (`took` is false). One case stays open by design: the POST arrived but neither its answer nor the check got through, so the words are restored although the service has them. If the owner taps Send again while that turn runs, the service answers 409 and the page then finds the first message in the saved chat and waits for its answer (case 6 covers the found path). If the turn had already finished, the second send is a new turn the owner chose.
- Cutting a healthy stream. Guard: the wake check runs only after the first event arrived (`began`) and aborts only when the service says the chat is no longer replying; case 4 proves a live stream is left alone. No timer-based abort is built, because the service sends nothing while the brain thinks or a tool runs.
- Extra reads. After a lost stream, or after coming back on screen during a reply, the page reads the whole chat every 2 s (the rate `openConsole` already uses) until the answer ends; a 200-message chat over mobile data is the worst case, bounded by the reply's length and by 30 minutes.
- Send stays held while the page waits for the saved answer (up to 30 minutes if the network stays down). The owner's words (/status, /pause, /restart sparkie, /help) still go through; leaving the chat ends the wait within 2 s.
- A console restart mid-turn loses `replying` (memory), so the saved chat comes back without the reply and the half-written text disappears. That is the truth; unchanged by this item.
- The test finds functions by name and indent. A function reformatted so its closing brace is not alone at its starting indent makes the test fail loudly (the AGENTS.md line says so). vm objects are another realm: use `assert.equal` on values, not `deepEqual` on arrays.
- Shadowing: do not name a local `live` in `sendConsole` (global `live()` exists); use `began`.
- Other items edit the same file (F18 near the sign-in code, A1's `/stop` in the composer). Edit by function name and re-read `sendConsole` first if A1 landed before this.
- The page is not part of the build id or the lock today (that is F5), so this change does not alter the build and needs no workflow re-validation; `node --check public/app.js` and the new test are its only gates.
- Real iOS behaviour (what Safari does to a stream on lock) cannot be simulated; the test proves the page's reaction to a cut, a quiet stream and a refused send, not the phone itself.

# put_state <saved> <live>: copies the saved state over the live state, except who is signed in and who has access.
# A live sessions.json, agents.json, passkeys.json or access.json that reads as JSON is left alone; one that is
# missing or can't be read is put back from the snapshot (so this can still end a lock-out).
put_state() {
  local f skip='' kept=''
  mkdir -p "$2"
  for f in sessions.json agents.json passkeys.json access.json; do
    if python3 -c 'import json, sys; sys.exit(0 if isinstance(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])), dict) else 1)' "$2/$f" 2>/dev/null; then
      skip="$skip --exclude=./$f"; kept="$kept $f"
    fi
  done
  tar -C "$1" $skip -cf - . | tar -C "$2" -xpf -
  [ -z "$kept" ] || echo "  Left as they are now (who is signed in and who has access):$kept"
}

c. Replace the three-line `--with-state` block (the `mkdir -p …; cp -a "$S/state/." …` one) with this single line:

Design in one line: the log's one true copy is ~/spark-console-src/docs/changes.md on Spark 2. The installer's Spark 2 half carries it across the source swap and adds one entry per install; restore.sh adds one "Undone" line. The tree's own docs/changes.md is only the heading.

Line numbers are for the installer as it is today; find each place by its text. A patched copy that passes the test is at /private/tmp/claude-502/-Users-akuppala-Documents-26aiRAG/aeda3f21-5bf5-4ab2-97c9-eb9169fa6d77/scratchpad/s6/host-on-portal.sh (session scratch; everything needed is also below).

STEP 1. New file docs/changes.md, exactly:

# Change log

One entry for every install of Spark Console, oldest first. Read the last ten before you change the code: what was
changed, why, and what was taken out again.

The installer writes each entry on Spark 2 (`change_entry` and `log_change` in `deploy/host-on-portal.sh`). Going back
a build adds an "Undone" line (`restore.sh`). Nothing else writes here, and a change never edits this file. The copy
that counts is the one on Spark 2, `~/spark-console-src/docs/changes.md`: each install keeps it and adds to it, whatever
the new source brings. A copy anywhere else may have no entries.

An entry says:

- **What and why:** the one line given when installing: `NOTE="what changed and why" bash deploy/host-on-portal.sh`.
  Say what went wrong on the way too. Never put a key or a password in it.
- **Gate:** when the whole suite passed for this build.
- **Files changed:** the files that differ from the source before it (40 at most are named).
- **Test blocks in the suite:** how many `test(` and `it(` blocks, and how many the build before had.
- **Result:** installed and answering, or it did not start, and the snapshot that holds the build before it.
- **Undone:** added later, if that snapshot was put back.

Before this log began (November 2026), what was changed and why is in `docs/analysis-2026-11-11/README.md` and
`docs/reviews-2026-11-11.md`.

STEP 2. deploy/host-on-portal.sh, header comment. Under the line `#   bash spark-console/deploy/host-on-portal.sh [user@host]` add:

#   NOTE="what changed and why" bash spark-console/deploy/host-on-portal.sh [user@host]
# NOTE (one line) goes into the change log kept with the source on Spark 2 (docs/changes.md): every install adds one
# entry there, and going back a build adds an "Undone" line.

STEP 3. Outer half. Right after the lock check (the line ending `installing now would switch every workflow off." >&2; exit 1; }`), add:

# The first lines of this install's entry in the change log (docs/changes.md, kept with the source on Spark 2): which
# build, what and why (NOTE, one line, given when installing), and when the whole suite passed for it. install.sh adds
# what changed and how it ended.
change_entry() {
  local note tested
  note="$(printf '%s' "${NOTE:-}" | tr '\r\n' '  ' | cut -c1-600 || true)"
  tested="$(python3 -c 'import json, sys; print(json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("testedAt", ""))' "$HERE/service/workflows.lock.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  echo "## ${STAMP:0:4}-${STAMP:4:2}-${STAMP:6:2}, build $API_BUILD"
  echo "- What and why: ${note:-not given (say it when installing: NOTE=\"what changed and why\")}"
  echo "- Gate: the whole suite passed for this build on ${tested:-a date the lock does not give}."
}
change_entry > "$STAGE/change.md"
[ -n "${NOTE:-}" ] || echo "Note: no NOTE was given, so the change log will not say what this update is for. Next time: NOTE=\"what changed and why\" bash $0" >&2

STEP 4. Ship it. In the copy line, change `tar -C "$STAGE" -cf - ui service install.sh source.tar |` to `tar -C "$STAGE" -cf - ui service install.sh source.tar change.md |`.

STEP 5. install.sh (inside the REMOTE heredoc). Right after the `socket_health() { … }` line, add:

# The change log kept with the source on this Spark (docs/changes.md): one entry per install, added here and never by
# the change itself.   log_change <source folder to write in> <how it ended> [<the source before it>]   (full paths)
# With the source before it, the log already on this Spark replaces the one that came with the new source (entries are
# only ever added here), and the entry says which files changed. Only a log that can't be carried over fails (so the
# old source stays); anything else that goes wrong is skipped.
log_change() {
  local to="$1/docs/changes.md" old="${3:-}" files n
  if [ -n "$old" ] && [ -f "$old/docs/changes.md" ]; then cp -p "$old/docs/changes.md" "$to" || return 1; fi
  [ -f "$IN/change.md" ] && [ -d "$1/docs" ] || return 0
  {
    echo; cat "$IN/change.md"
    if [ -n "$old" ] && [ -d "$old" ]; then
      files=$(cd "$1" && find . -type f ! -path ./docs/changes.md | sed 's|^\./||' | sort | while read -r f; do cmp -s "$f" "$old/$f" || echo "$f"; done) || true
      n=$(printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep -c . || true)
      echo "- Files changed: $n"
      printf '%s\n' "$files" | grep . | head -40 | sed 's/^/  - /' || true
      [ "$n" -le 40 ] || echo "  - and $((n - 40)) more"
      echo "- Test blocks in the suite: $(cat "$1"/test/*.test.mjs 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*(test|it)\(' || true) (the build before had $(cat "$old"/test/*.test.mjs 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*(test|it)\(' || true))"
    fi
    echo "- Result: $2${SNAP:+ The build before it is saved as ${SNAP##*/}.}"
  } >> "$to" || true
  return 0
}

Keep the function's closing `}` at the start of its line and everything inside indented: the test cuts the function out by that shape. Same for change_entry.

STEP 6. restore.sh (inside the RESTORE heredoc). After the `--with-state` block's closing `fi` and before `systemctl --user daemon-reload`, add:

# The change log kept with the source (docs/changes.md): one line saying this build was taken out again. It never
# stops a restore.
LOG="$HOME/spark-console-src/docs/changes.md"
if [ -f "$LOG" ]; then echo "- Undone $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d): the build saved as ${S##*/} was put back." >> "$LOG" || true; fi

This one place covers undo_update, the installer's own put-back, and a restore by hand.

STEP 7. A build that did not start. In the `if [ -z "$HEALTHY" ]` block, right after the `journalctl … || true` line and before the "no earlier install" check, add:

  log_change "$HOME/spark-console-src" 'it did not start.' || true

STEP 8. A build that started. In the source swap chain, between the tar extract and the first `mv`:

  rm -rf "$SRC.new" "$SRC.old" && mkdir -p "$SRC.new" && tar --warning=no-unknown-keyword -C "$SRC.new" -xf "$IN/source.tar" \
    && log_change "$SRC.new" 'installed and answering.' "$SRC" \
    && { [ ! -d "$SRC" ] || mv "$SRC" "$SRC.old"; } && mv "$SRC.new" "$SRC" && rm -rf "$SRC.old" \

log_change returns non-zero only when the old log could not be copied into the new source; then the swap is skipped, the existing line "NOTE: couldn't keep the source in … (the install itself is fine)." prints, and the old source with its log stays.

WORDS THE OWNER SEES
- Only when no NOTE was given, on the installing terminal: `Note: no NOTE was given, so the change log will not say what this update is for. Next time: NOTE="what changed and why" bash deploy/host-on-portal.sh`. The install goes on; a missing note never refuses an install.
- An entry on Spark 2 reads:
  ## 2026-11-12, build 1a2b3c4d5e6f
  - What and why: <the NOTE, one line, 600 characters at most>
  - Gate: the whole suite passed for this build on 2026-11-12T01:42:56.625Z.
  - Files changed: 3
    - service/src/20-words.mjs
    - …
  - Test blocks in the suite: 391 (the build before had 383)
  - Result: installed and answering. The build before it is saved as 20261112T034500Z.
  and, if it is taken out later: `- Undone 2026-11-13: the build saved as 20261112T034500Z was put back.`
- A build that did not start gets the first three lines, then `- Result: it did not start. The build before it is saved as <stamp>.`, then restore.sh's Undone line.

IF OTHER ITEMS LANDED FIRST
- F4 or H1 (installer goes back by itself, go-back.sh): call `log_change "$HOME/spark-console-src" '<the plain reason F4 prints>' || true` once on every path that gives up on the new build, before restore.sh runs. Keep the Undone line after restore.sh's put_back calls.
- S5 (update record): if it already gave the installer a note input, use that same input for change_entry instead of adding NOTE. One note, two records.
- S11 (source kept and restored): if the swap is skipped in `local` mode, call `log_change "$SRC" 'installed and answering.'` there (no third argument). A restored source must keep the Spark 2 log, and any hash of the source must leave docs/changes.md out.

CUT, ON PURPOSE
- No new action, no line in sparkie_setup (S5 does the last five), no service code. Sparkie reads the file once console_code (M5) exists; change_console (M7) reads the last entries then.
- No copy of the log back to the Mac, no merge of two logs, no secret masking in bash, no refusal without a note, no build hashing in restore.sh, no list of test titles.
- No copy of Claude's notes into the tree; that is D9 (docs/handoff.md).

- It sits in the install and restore paths. Guard: every new call is best effort (`|| true` inside and at the call), a missing note never refuses an install, and the Undone line cannot stop a restore. Only a log that cannot be carried over does anything: it skips the source swap, which already has its own "the install itself is fine" line.
- Losing the log at the swap. Guard: the old log is copied into the new source before the old source is moved, and a failed copy leaves the old source in place. The test covers carry-over, the no-entry case and the failed copy.

Guard: an explicit environment (temporary HOME, stand-ins first on PATH, no session variables) and an assert that `systemctl` resolves to the stand-in before the script runs. Do not loosen that environment.

specs.risk:
1. The stand-in Sparks report a constant uptime, so the worked-out boot time drifts forward with the clock. Guard: the boot on record moves later on every reading (rule b), so only a gap of more than 2 minutes between two readings of an online stand-in Spark could look like a restart. Not seen in the scratch runs. If a full-suite run ever shows an `inferred` event in a fleet that seeded none, do not loosen the rule: make the stand-in's default uptime advance (in test/mock/worker.py add the age of `$MOCK_DIR/pids.json` to `uptimeSeconds`; values set through `status.json` stay as written, dark.test asserts them exactly).

2. Using `Date.now()` instead of `Date.parse(now)` would write false pairs in pause, passkey and internet tests (they move `Date.now()` by up to 13 hours). Guard: rule a, and pause.test in the run list.

3. The back-dated offline event: `fleet_events {since}` will not show it for a later `since`, and events are no longer strictly time-ordered. `cameBack`, `darkPeriods` and `healApp` pair by position and read the times, so they work; `darkPeriods` then lists the spell from "last seen" with "no reading near the time it went dark". Guard: R23 says so; `inferred: true` and the fleet-note words mark it.

4. A forward clock step of more than 2 minutes on Spark 2 would look like one restart of every online Spark. Bounded: two events per Spark, and only should-run entries already down with exit 255 get a bring-back (twice in 6 hours, "froze it" guard). The boot on record never moves earlier, so a wrong early clock cannot set this up.

5. The "it may be what froze it" guard measures from the inferred offline time, which is the last-seen time on file and can be older than the real one. It errs toward holding when the file is fresh and can miss when the file is older than the last bring-back. Accepted; the twice-in-6-hours limit still applies.

6. Spark 2 itself: every restart of Spark 2 is unwatched, so it gets the pair too. True and harmless (nothing on the should-run list is on Spark 2; `maybeHeal` returns early there); it gives the owner a record of when Spark 2 was down.

7. Still not covered, on purpose: a clean power-off that leaves exit 0, 137 or 143 (backlog), and a model with no entry on the should-run list.

- Taking the wrong thing off the list. Guard: only stops the operation itself recorded, and only when that Spark answered and the container is not running there; an entry that was already held before the start is left alone, as a finished start leaves it.

A. deploy/host-on-portal.sh, outer script, the `if [ "$HOST" = local ]; then` block: after `SSH=(on_spark2)` add

  export INSTALL_FROM="$HERE"
(No argument-count change. Over SSH the variable is absent, so a Mac install swaps as today.)

B. install.sh heredoc, after the `REL=` line add
SRC="$HOME/spark-console-src"
# The source of the build that is installed now, as one file. Each install keeps its own here once it answers, and the
# next install's snapshot takes it, so going back a build can put that build's source back too.
KEPT="$HOME/.local/share/spark-console/installed-source.tar"

C. Snapshot block, right after `save "$STATE" state`:
    if [ -f "$KEPT" ]; then cp -p "$KEPT" "$SNAP/source.tar"; fi
Do NOT save the live ~/spark-console-src there (see evidence). No fallback when $KEPT is missing.

D. restore.sh heredoc. Header comment: say it also puts this build's source back in ~/spark-console-src and keeps the tree that was there as ~/spark-console-src.undone-<time>. Then, directly after `systemctl --user restart spark-console-api` and before the `for _ in $(seq 1 20)` loop:
SRC="$HOME/spark-console-src"; KEPT="$HOME/.local/share/spark-console/installed-source.tar"
if [ "${KEEP_SOURCE:-}" = 1 ]; then :
elif [ -f "$S/source.tar" ]; then
  AWAY=''; [ ! -d "$SRC" ] || AWAY="$SRC.undone-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
  rm -rf "$SRC.back" && mkdir -p "$SRC.back" && tar -C "$SRC.back" -xf "$S/source.tar" 2>/dev/null \
    && { [ -z "$AWAY" ] || mv "$SRC" "$AWAY"; } && mv "$SRC.back" "$SRC" && cp -p "$S/source.tar" "$KEPT" \
    && echo "  Source: $SRC is this build's source again.${AWAY:+ What was there is kept in $AWAY.}" \
    || echo "  NOTE: couldn't put the source back in $SRC. The install itself is back." >&2
else
  rm -f "$KEPT"
  echo "  NOTE: this snapshot holds no source, so $SRC was left as it is. It may not be the code that runs now."
fi
Keep it one and-or chain ending in `|| echo` (the script is `set -e`; this step must never stop a restore). No `--warning` flag here: restore.sh must stay runnable by the test on macOS. Undone trees are time-named and never removed.

E. install.sh, the installer's own go-back: `if bash "$SNAP/restore.sh" >&2; then` becomes `if KEEP_SOURCE=1 bash "$SNAP/restore.sh" >&2; then` (the new build never ran, so the tree the owner or Sparkie is working in stays put and $KEPT is still right). # The source of the build now running. One copy is kept as a file (the next install's snapshot takes it), and the tree

    || { rm -f "$KEPT" "$KEPT.new"; echo "  NOTE: couldn't keep a copy of this build's source for going back (the install itself is fine)."; }
  if [ -n "${INSTALL_FROM:-}" ] && [ "$INSTALL_FROM" -ef "$SRC" ]; then
    echo "  source: $SRC (installed from this folder, so it was left as it is)"
  else
    <the existing rm/mkdir/tar/mv/mv/rm chain and its two echo lines, unchanged, minus its own SRC= line>
  fi
fi

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Puts back the Spark Console build from before the last update, by hand, when Spark Console doesn't answer (when it
# does, type /undo update in your chat instead). It runs the newest complete snapshot's restore.sh: the page, the
# service and its unit are put back and the service is restarted. People, chats and settings stay as they are.
# It never touches SSH, Tailscale, the firewall, users or any model, and needs no sudo.
#   bash ~/.local/share/spark-console/go-back.sh
# Every install copies this file there (deploy/host-on-portal.sh); RECOVERY.txt beside it lists the other steps.
set -euo pipefail
[ $# -eq 0 ] || { echo "Usage: bash $0   (no options: it puts back the build's files only)" >&2; exit 2; }
REL="$HOME/.local/share/spark-console/releases"
last=''
for d in "$REL"/[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]T[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]Z; do
  if [ -f "$d/restore.sh" ]; then last="$d"; fi
done
[ -n "$last" ] || { echo "There's no earlier build to go back to on this Spark (nothing complete in $REL)." >&2; exit 1; }
echo "Going back to the build saved before the update on ${last##*/} ..."
exec bash "$last/restore.sh"
```

specs.risk:
1. **Fighting the owner.** If the owner works by hand on Spark 2 after a failed switch while the mark is set, the keeper may remove the container and run the saved setup once the brain has been down about 2 to 3 minutes.
   - Guards: it acts only with the mark; only after `HEAL_SETTLE_MS`; never while a brain job, restart or claim is on Spark 2; at most twice in 6 hours, then the mark is cleared. The owner's Stop clears the mark. `/pause` or turning automatic restarts off stops it.
   - Left open: a stale mark can survive if healing is paused the whole time the brain was fixed by hand and then stopped by hand again. Worst case is one unwanted start of the owner's own setup.
2. **Docker not answering reads as a missing container.** `mainStatusScript` turns a failed `docker inspect` into `missing`. A Docker outage longer than the settle time gives one misleading notice, or two used tries if the mark is set. F6's marker is the proper fix; nothing was added here.
3. **First test to run a brain start on the stand-in fleet.** I checked `mainRunCommand`, the overlay step and the stand-in `docker run` by reading only. If the start fails there for a stand-in reason, fix the stand-in data, not `startMain`.
4. **The mark must never block or break a start.** `markBrainLeftDown` catches everything, and reads with `readKept` so a failed read is never written over as empty. `brainLeftDown` reads false on any error, which means no keeper action.
5. **The notices name a word that refuses today.** Build F3 first, and keep the notice text in step with the wording F3 ships.
6. **F3 may reuse `startMain` for a missing container from the word.** That call must not set `noStops` unless F3 wants it. If F3 added a helper that creates the `main-start` job, the keeper should call it with the extra fields instead of a third copy.
7. **No memory check (R2).** The keeper restarts the setup that ran minutes earlier and refuses whenever anything would stop, copy or download. The gap is written into R2's "Today" note. Add the check when F1 gives the stand-in fleet its own memory file.
8. **Other builders are editing the tree tonight.** `docs/architecture.md` (R37), `16-actions.mjs`, `14-chats.mjs` and the stand-in `docker` all changed during this check. Re-read each rule row before editing it; no existing test is touched.
9. **Existing tests.** The default settle is 120 s, so `words.test.mjs`, which leaves the brain exited for under a minute with no mark, sees at most one extra notice on a very slow machine. Nothing there counts notices.

1. A Spark whose Docker default log driver is not json-file or local would refuse `--log-opt max-size` and the start would fail. For the brain that is serious: `startMain` removes the old container before `docker run`, so a refused run leaves Sparkie down. Guard: `LOG_CAP` names the driver (`--log-driver json-file`), which makes both options valid on any daemon and keeps `docker logs` and `container_logs` working. This is the one addition beyond the review's two flags, and nobody has to check the Sparks' daemon settings.
2. Flags placed after the image would be handed to the engine and break every start. Guard: spread them right after `'-d'`; the test asserts they come before `--entrypoint`.
3. Both start workflows get a new version. Guard: expected for Batch 5; one lock run for the batch, the five versions printed before and after, and the live start-check-stop in ownerStep. `restart_model` is unchanged, so crash restarts are unaffected.
